column2: The planning layer — authorship taken from the superscriptions alone, the arc across the collections, the preaching traps, and the unit plan the series is built on.

Eight macro-arguments the eleven runs jointly demonstrate. Proverbs is not an anthology that later acquired a frame but a designed book, and the design shows in three registers that do not depend on each other.
The original sweep: all eighteen units at proportional depth with a cross-passage synthesis. The seedbed the solo digs grew from.
The nine-sermon series plan, and the backbone of the opening survey sermon — a whole-book view with no single base text.
Sermon 1 backbone — moving the congregation from approaching Proverbs as advice for the competent to receiving it as a gift for the gullible.
Sermon 2 backbone — out of both passivity and self-reliance into asking; the middle verb of the three, and the one most often skipped because it feels least like effort.
The preamble bracketed by a single word-pair — ḥokmâ ûmûsār at verse 2 and again at verse 7 — and the bracket is the argument.
One sentence, twenty-two verses: three conditions, then, for, then, for, and two purpose-infinitives of rescue. The chapter that sets the agenda for chapters 3–7.
The frame entire. Chapter 2 announces a programme and chapters 3–7 execute it in order; ten lectures and five interludes, with Wisdom and Folly calling from the same height in chapter 9.
Solomon I entire. The received text divides it into four paragraphs — none of them where this project had been cutting — and the Greek carries nineteen verse-units the Hebrew has not.
The Words of the Wise. Masoretic paragraphing fifteen times denser than Solomon I, which turns out to be the explanation the project had been missing.
Solomon II entire. Three silences nest inside one another — the king for 91 verses, the divine name for 65, the righteous and wicked for 57 — with chapters 26–27 inside all three.
Agur and Lemuel. Every block boundary the Greek rearrangement creates falls where the received Hebrew already marks a paragraph: five seams, five markers.
The closing acrostic. Proverbs says the same thing, in the same words, about finding Wisdom and finding a wife — and this poem asks that question one last time.
Solomon I, first half. The righteous/wicked pair falls away almost exactly as the divine name takes over, and the antithetical form loosens with them.
Solomon I, second half. All four sub-collections counted on one scheme for the first time — they alternate rather than progress.
Solomon II, first half. Kābēd — glory, honour, weight — as the section’s Leitwort, and 25:21 as the Covenant Code’s enemy-duty, where both Jesus and Paul go for love of enemies.
Solomon II, second half. A four-fold refrain-chain on the rise and fall of the righteous and the wicked, and the golden-calf allusion behind 29:18.
Ansberry’s collection scheme for Proverbs 10–29 tested against the text before the sweeps began. It stands — with three corrections and one caution.
Thirty-three manual library returns graded against the open questions of the 1:1–7, Proverbs 2 and 1:8–9:18 reports. The status board near the top overrides every other status statement.
Twenty answers audited: eleven adopted as given, six with qualification, three rejected — including one claim the Hebrew text refutes outright.

The whole book read against the Greek at last. Forty-eight lettered pluses and twenty-four Hebrew verses with no Greek counterpart — concentrated, not scattered: eighteen in the frame, none at all in 30–31.

The forest, for use while working in the wood. A one-page spine of the book’s argument, then one card per sermon — the strongest finding, the Big Question’s answer, the Christ line and the trap. Compression only; no new findings.
Sermon 4 backbone — “Who is calling?” Two voices issue the identical invitation from the same street (9:4 = 9:16), the father falls silent at 7:27, and Wisdom takes his own formula at 8:32.

Sermon 5 backbone — the world sorted, the crest at chapter 16, and the auditor disqualified. Structure follows the four transmitted paragraphs, not the chapter divisions; 15:33/16:1 is explicitly not the hinge.
Sermon 6 backbone — borrowed wisdom re-founded on trust at 22:19, and tested where it cannot be faked: on behalf of people with no advocate. Highest moralism risk in the series, with the guard named.

Sermon 7 backbone — the three nested silences preached as pedagogy, the hinge at the paragraph crossing 27:27/28:1, and the honour thread from 25:27 to 29:23. Four movements on transmitted paragraph boundaries.
Sermon 8 backbone — the book’s last sage says he never learned wisdom, and the unit turns on a single paragraph marker: hand on the mouth (30:32) becomes open your mouth (31:8, 9).
Sermon 9 backbone, closing the series — one imperative in twenty-two verses, it is the book’s last word, and it is addressed to the observer: recognise wisdom in another and say so publicly.
